currentContext.business: Anup designs and fabricates custom-engineered process equipment - Shell & Tube Heat Exchangers, Reactors, Pressure Vessels, Columns & Towers, Industrial Centrifuges, Silos and Storage Tanks - for process industries including Oil & Gas, Petrochemicals, LNG, Fertilisers, Chemicals, Power, Hydrogen, Water and Paper & Pulp; BRSR classifies 99.87% of turnover under a single activity, 'Fabrication of metal and metal products' (NIC 28230). Shell & Tube Heat Exchangers have historically been the flagship product and, per the MD&A segment-wise commentary, contributed approximately 70% of annual revenue, with the mix broadening into Reactors, Pressure Vessels and Columns & Towers after the Kheda facility was commissioned. Alongside manufacturing, the Company has established a dedicated Technical Services Division offering health assessment and integrity evaluation, NDE services, technical consulting and engineering, heat-exchanger retubing and equipment repair, component replacement and life-extension, and laboratory testing / failure analysis, and it made its first foray into the Critical Equipment Business during FY 2025-26.

Process equipment (manufacturing): Air Cooled Heat Exchangers (first order in FY26)
Critical / complex equipment (incl. Solid Inconel 200MT single-piece equipment)
Technical Services Division: Laboratory Testing, Failure Analysis & Metallurgical Investigations

currentContext.expansion: Capacity build-out is the central operating story of FY 2025-26 and is described as essentially complete. Phase II of the expansion at the Kheda (Gujarat) manufacturing facility was successfully completed during the year, described in the MD&A as having 'enhanced production capacity, operational efficiency, and manufacturing flexibility'; the MD & CEO message quantifies it: 'We have completed our phase 2 expansion at Kheda increasing the capacity to 8000MT per year, with a revenue capacity of Rs 400 Cr to Rs 450 Cr.' The Kheda plant is described as new, strategically located close to the National Highway, and 'now fully operational', enabling manufacture of larger and heavier process equipment and a shift of mix towards Reactors, Pressure Vessels, Columns & Towers and other large-scale fabricated equipment. The second leg of the expansion was inorganic: Mabel Engineers Private Limited, the 100%-owned manufacturing subsidiary in Tamil Nadu (acquired June 19, 2024), had its operations successfully integrated and stabilised during FY26, adding southern-India geographic presence and Silos, Storage Tanks and Process Vessels to the portfolio. A design office at Vadodara has stabilised, supports execution and has recently started taking small external assignments. Taken together, the MD & CEO states that 'With these installed capacities at our 3 manufacturing locations, ie. Ahmedabad, Kheda and Mabel Engineers, we have a capacity capable of delivering revenue up to Rs 1200 Cr per year' - i.e. the stated posture for FY27 is to sweat capacity already created rather than to announce a new project; no new expansion project, commissioning date or capex quantum for a future project is disclosed anywhere in the routed bundle. Energy assets: a windmill of 750 KW capacity and a solar plant of 1790 KW capacity are installed, set off against energy consumed in manufacturing units (Annexure D, Conservation of Energy); the MD notes both Gujarat manufacturing facilities have rooftop solar and a windmill meeting about 40% of electricity requirement. BRSR Section A item 18 (standalone boundary) discloses only a location count - 2 plants and 1 office in India, none international - with no capacity figures; note this conflicts in appearance with the 3 manufacturing locations cited by the MD, because Mabel sits outside the standalone BRSR boundary. BRSR Principle 2 discloses that 4.85% of total capex investment in FY 2025-26 (0% in FY 2024-25) went into specific technologies improving environmental and social impacts, with R&D at 0% in both years - a percentage only, no rupee amount, and it is not a NAMED DISCLOSURE, so it is deliberately excluded from capex_disclosed. Annexure D also records that an amount was invested in energy-conservation equipment but the sentence is truncated mid-figure ('An amount of Rs 1' - text cut off), so that quantum is unusable. DEFECT NOTE on the NAMED DISCLOSURE block supplied for capital commitments: the same Note 27 appears twice, tagged [page 74] and [page 109], with identical figures 932.14 and 1,333.20. The page-74 header is truncated at 'As at' with no date at all; the page-109 header reads 'As at March 31, 2026'. Both headers also carry conflicting unit candidates - '(Rs in Lakhs) | (In Millions)' - although the note body itself states '(Rs in Lakhs)' twice, which is what has been used. Because only ONE column date is readable while TWO figures are printed, only the current-year figure has been emitted (932.14, as at 31 March 2026, matching the sole readable date and the customary first-column position); the second figure, 1,333.20, is the undated comparative and has been OMITTED rather than guessed. Verbatim reproduction of the block as supplied: '[page 74] (Rs in Lakhs) | (In Millions) | for the year ended March 31, 2026 | As at / Note 27 : Capital Commitment and Other Commitments / (Rs in Lakhs) / (a) Capital Commitments / (i) Estimated amount of Contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for (Net of advances) / 932.14 / 1,333.20' and '[page 109] (Rs in Lakhs) | (In Millions) | for the year ended March 31, 2026 | As at March 31, 2026 / Note 27 : Capital Commitment and Other Commitments / (Rs in Lakhs) / (a) Capital Commitments / (i) Estimated amount of Contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for (Net of advances) / 932.14 / 1,333.20'. Also note the page-74 tag is anomalous: per the annual report's own contents page, the Standalone Financial Statements begin at page 97, so a Note 27 appearing at page 74 falls inside the Corporate Governance Report page range - the duplicate is most likely the standalone/consolidated pair or a page-numbering artefact of the extractor, and it is flagged rather than resolved.

Rs 769 Cr to be executed based on the delivery plans.'|LABEL INCONSISTENCY (flagged, not resolved): the same Rs 769 Cr figure is described three different ways in the same annual report - 'opening Order Book' (Directors' Report), 'order pipeline' (MD&A) and 'pending order book' (MD & CEO message). The as-of date is stated only once, as on March 31, 2026.|'Order booking has surely improved, and with a good enquiry pipeline, we see good business opportunities for this year and the next year. Having said that, we will be very judicious in booking new orders considering the current high input costs.'|Order composition is shifting to large-sized complex projects with long execution cycles, average 12-14 months, which management says will cause quarter-on-quarter fluctuations that broadly normalise over the year.|New order categories won for the first time in FY26: Nuclear, Thermal Power, Clean Energy Storage technology (European technology company), Skids, and Air Cooled Heat Exchangers.|Technical Services: over 10 orders executed in FY26.

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict, sea-route closure and trade/tariff regimes hitting an export-heavy order book
risks.note: The MD&A 'Threats' paragraph names the evolving geopolitical landscape, ongoing regional conflicts, supply chain disruptions and uncertainties from global trade policies and tariff regimes as challenges 'for manufacturers with significant export and import exposure', potentially affecting project execution timelines, material availability, logistics costs and overall operations. This is not theoretical for Anup: the MD & CEO records that in the last few weeks of FY26 critical materials 'not finding ways' and curtailed industrial gas supply restricted the pace of manufacturing, and that a sizeable accumulation of finished goods due to non-availability of shipping lines limited shop-floor flow and impacted progress of new work.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility (especially steel) and elevated input costs on long-cycle fixed-price orders
risks.note: The MD & CEO cites volatility in raw material pricing especially steel, energy prices and higher logistics costs, and states the Company will be 'very judicious in booking new orders considering the current high input costs'. With average execution cycles of 12-14 months on large complex projects, input-cost movement between quotation and delivery is a structural margin risk; management also flags that labour, freight and royalty will remain relatively higher in the new order mix.

risks.risk: Availability of skilled operators and technical personnel
risks.note: Explicitly flagged in MD&A 'Threats': the business involves the design and manufacture of highly engineered, custom-built equipment, 'making the availability of a skilled workforce a critical success factor', and the industry continues to face challenges attracting and retaining skilled operators and technical personnel required to support growing demand. Mitigation stated is automation, digitalisation and productivity improvement plus workforce development.

risks.risk: Execution risk and earnings lumpiness from large, complex, long-cycle projects
risks.note: Management states that with the large-sized Kheda facility fully operational the Company is focused on taking large-sized complex projects with long execution cycles (average 12-14 months), so 'it is natural that you will see fluctuations in quarter-on-quarter numbers'. Execution slippage is already visible: the MD notes Mabel's contribution 'would have been better if not for some site projects which got prolonged than expected due to technical changes'. First-time entries into Nuclear, Thermal Power, Clean Energy Storage, Skids and Air Cooled Heat Exchangers add first-of-a-kind execution risk.

BRSR item 19 discloses exports at 48.2% of total turnover in the reporting year, across 12 countries and 13 Indian states, and the MD states the export:domestic ratio continued at 50:50 as a matter of strategic intent. Roughly half of turnover is therefore exposed to cross-border logistics, tariff regimes, currency and the Middle East demand cycle that the MD&A identifies as the key export opportunity.

BRSR discloses one business activity - 'Fabrication of metal and metal products' - at 99.87% of turnover, and one product line (Heat Exchanger, Pressure Vessels, Towers, Reactors, Column and Centrifuges, NIC 28230) also at 99.87%. Within that, Shell & Tube Heat Exchangers have historically been approximately 70% of annual revenue, projected to moderate to approximately 60% in the current year - i.e. diversification is under way but concentration remains high.

risks.risk: End-market cyclicality - dependence on process-industry capital expenditure
risks.note: Demand is a derived function of capex by Oil & Gas, Petrochemicals, Fertilisers, Hydrogen, Power and LNG customers; MD&A explicitly grounds the outlook in 'healthy capital expenditure across key end-user industries' and 'significant greenfield and brownfield investments'. A capex pause in these industries, or a faster-than-expected transition away from Oil & Gas, transmits directly to order inflow.

risks.risk: Worker safety exposure in a contract-labour-heavy fabrication workforce
risks.note: BRSR Principle 3 reports 13 total recordable work-related injuries to workers in FY 2025-26 (6 in FY 2024-25) and one worker fatality in FY 2024-25 (none in FY 2025-26), while Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate is reported as 0 for both employees and workers in both years - an internal inconsistency worth noting. Of the 13 affected workers in FY26 and 6 in FY25, the number rehabilitated or placed in suitable employment is reported as 0. The workforce structure concentrates this risk: 0 permanent workers versus 783 other-than-permanent workers (100% male) against 391 permanent employees.

risks.risk: Risk governance is framework-only, with no named enterprise risk register disclosed
risks.note: The MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' section and the Directors' Report 'Risk Management Policy' section are near-identical boilerplate describing a Risk Management Committee of the Board, a Risk Management Policy, an Internal Audit Department facilitating identification/assessment/monitoring/mitigation, and annual Audit Committee review - but no specific risk is named, scored or quantified anywhere in either section. The BRSR material responsible-business-conduct issues table, which would normally carry the named risk/opportunity rows, is truncated in the routed material (only rows 7 Human Capital Management and 8 Diversity and Inclusion survive, both classified 'Opportunity').

one-line thesis: Anup Engineering is executing a strategic transformation from a domestic heat exchanger specialist to a diversified process equipment manufacturer with expanded capacity at Kheda, targeting higher-margin exotic metallurgy and export markets, despite near-term margin pressure from raw material spikes. The company is poised for 25%+ CAGR over 3 years, supported by a robust order book and a new facility designed for complex, high-value equipment.
financial scorecard: rev:153cr (+8% YoY); EBITDA:30cr (19.6% margin); PAT:unstated; orderbook:536cr; netdebt:20-25cr (temporary)
guidance: H2 FY23 revenue guidance of Rs. 225cr; full-year FY23 revenue expected to be slightly below Rs. 400cr; 30% annualized growth; FY24 margin recovery to 24-25%; 25%+ CAGR over next 3 years; Kheda Phase-1 to contribute Rs. 75-100cr in FY24
order book & pipeline: Rs. 536cr as of Q2FY23; Rs. 300cr booked in H1; similar traction expected in H2; includes orders specifically for Kheda facility; 17% export mix currently
segment / subsidiary detail: Heat exchangers: ~75% of current portfolio; targeting reduction to 60%; reactors and pressure vessels: primary focus for Kheda; exotic metallurgy (titanium, etc.): key growth driver; clean room equipment: active at Odhav; hydrogen equipment: emerging focus
growth verticals / optionality: Kheda Phase-1 (1.5 bays) commissioning in Q4FY23; Phases 2 and 3 targeting FY25 and FY26; potential for 7 total bays at Kheda; exploration of new verticals via Rishi Kapoor's strategic team; licensing of proprietary tech (e.g., Lummus Helix); export market expansion; hydrogen equipment development
margins & cost dynamics: Q2 FY23 EBITDA margin: 19.6%; H1 margin: 11.8% due to raw material spike (nickel alloys up 200%); margins to normalize to 24-25% from Q1FY24 as new orders (post-spike) have restored historical pricing; cost recovery efforts via design efficiency and negotiation mitigated impact
capex / expansion: Kheda Phase-1 CAPEX: Rs. 115cr; spent Rs. 60cr to date; total funding requirement for CAPEX and WC: Rs. 20-25cr; debt-funded; future phases to follow; Odhav clean room and heavy bay already operational
capital allocation: Debt financing for Kheda CAPEX and working capital (Rs. 20-25cr); zero-debt philosophy maintained as goal; temporary debt for cash flow mismatch; no equity raise planned; focus on internal cash generation post-ramp-up; Kheda breakeven at Rs. 75cr revenue for Phase-1
risks & watch-items: Raw material price volatility; execution risk at new Kheda facility; delays in customer qualification for exports; maintaining on-time delivery during rapid scale-up; dependence on PSU tenders; integration of new technical capabilities; potential dilution of quality standards; geopolitical supply chain shifts impacting export demand
management quality / tone: Confident, strategic, and disciplined; leadership transition (Regie Dsouza) viewed positively; strong emphasis on operational excellence, on-time delivery, and quality; transparent about near-term margin headwinds; clear roadmap for diversification and export growth; cautious on pace of Kheda ramp-up to preserve reputation; proactive on technology licensing and team building
non-obvious takeaways: Kheda's 17m hook height and 200m length are uniquely suited for heavy, large-diameter equipment — a rare capability in India; export growth is not from scratch — Regie brings pre-existing global customer relationships; the 35cr loan to subsidiary is a contra-entry in consolidated books, not real debt; Rishi Kapoor's separate team is not a distraction but a strategic incubator to protect Anup's focus; 100% on-time delivery is a core competitive moat being preserved even during expansion

hero.oneLiner: The Anup Engineering Limited is a Gujarat-based designer and manufacturer of highly engineered, custom-built process equipment - heat exchangers, pressure vessels, reactors, columns and centrifuges - for chemical, petrochemical, refinery, fertiliser and energy customers in India and export markets.
